  "text": "The first time the upstairs neighbor knocked, Mara pretended not to be home.

The second time, he left a small brass key in an envelope beneath her door. On the envelope he had written: For the roof. Tomatoes need water while I’m away.

She had lived in the building for eleven months. They had exchanged perhaps six sentences, mostly about parcels.

On Tuesday evening she tried the key.

There were no tomatoes. There were twelve black buckets containing soil and brittle stalks, a folding chair, and a watering can with a cracked handle. Beyond the parapet, the laundromat sign flashed against the windows opposite.

She watered the buckets anyway.

He returned on Sunday carrying a suitcase held shut with a belt.

“Your tomatoes are dead,” she told him.

“Yes,” he said. “I wondered.”

“You could have mentioned that.”

He looked down at the suitcase. “I usually go up there with my wife.”

Mara had never seen his wife. She waited, but he only asked for the key.

That evening she found an unopened packet of radish seeds in her kitchen drawer. She had bought them in March, imagining a different sort of summer.

She took them upstairs.

“Wrong season, probably,” she said when he opened the door.

He studied the packet. “We can check.”

They planted two buckets and left the others alone. He showed her where the tap was hidden behind a loose board.

On her way down, Mara remembered the watering can.

“I’ve got some tape for that handle.”

“Bring it next time,” he said.

She kept the key."
